justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly bullish near-term outlook anchored to recent price action and prevailing momentum. For the one-day estimate, I leaned heavily on the last observed price level and short-term technical continuity, assuming no major overnight catalyst would disrupt the trend. The slight upward drift in the one-week and one-month estimates reflects a mild positive bias consistent with broader market conditions, earnings expectations, or sector trends that were in play at the time of the forecast. Each successive horizon adds a small increment to the point estimate, representing the compounding effect of a gradual drift assumption rather than any sharp directional call.

The confidence interval widths widen progressively across horizons in a manner consistent with standard diffusion uncertainty — the further out you forecast, the more time there is for new information to accumulate and push prices away from the current trajectory. The one-day interval is relatively tight, reflecting that intraday or overnight volatility is bounded in most normal market conditions. By one month, the interval spans roughly 67 points, acknowledging that macro shifts, earnings releases, sector rotations, or changes in interest rate expectations could meaningfully alter the price path. Implied volatility levels and recent realized volatility in the underlying asset also informed how wide I set these bands.

There are several specific risks that could push outcomes outside these intervals in either direction. On the upside, a strong earnings surprise, a favorable macro data release such as lower-than-expected inflation, or a sudden wave of institutional buying could push the price well above the upper bound of the one-month range. On the downside, a risk-off event — geopolitical escalation, a Federal Reserve policy surprise, or a broader equity market selloff — could breach the lower bound. Liquidity crunches or unexpected news specific to the underlying company or sector represent tail risks that are by definition underweighted in any interval built on historical volatility patterns, meaning true tail outcomes remain possible even outside the 90% confidence bands I provided.
